First, we note that $m=0$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

We multiply both sides of the equation by ${m}^{3},$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3m-1}{{m}^{3}}+\frac{m+2}{{m}^{3}} & =\frac{2m+3}{{m}^{3}} \\ {m}^{3}\cdot (\frac{3m-1}{{m}^{3}}+\frac{m+2}{{m}^{3}}) & ={m}^{3}\cdot (\frac{2m+3}{{m}^{3}}) \\ {m}^{3}\cdot \frac{3m-1}{{m}^{3}}+{m}^{3}\cdot \frac{m+2}{{m}^{3}} & ={m}^{3}\cdot \frac{2m+3}{{m}^{3}} \\ \cancel{{m}^{3}}\cdot \frac{3m-1}{\cancel{{m}^{3}}}+\cancel{{m}^{3}}\cdot \frac{m+2}{\cancel{{m}^{3}}} & =\cancel{{m}^{3}}\cdot \frac{2m+3}{\cancel{{m}^{3}}} \\ 3m-1+m+2 & =2m+3\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $m,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3m-1+m+2 & =2m+3 \\ 4m+1 & =2m+3 \\ 4m-2m & =3-1 \\ 2m & =2 \\ m & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $m=0$ as a solution. But since $m=1\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $m=1.$
